questions.question:
Put these tasks in the correct order: (1) write the code, (2) gather requirements, (3) test/debug, (4) create the algorithm.
A. 2, 1, 4, 3
B. 1, 2, 4, 3
C. 2, 4, 1, 3
D. 4, 2, 1, 3

A program runs, but the total it shows is wrong because of a mistake in its instructions. What should the programmer do?
A. Debug it: find and fix the error
B. Delete the algorithm
C. Convert it to machine language
D. Deploy it right away

Mia wants a friend to understand her plan for a program before any code is written, and her friend knows no programming language. Which tool fits best?
A. Bytecode
B. Assembly language
C. Machine language
D. Pseudocode

Which statement best compares high-level and low-level languages?
A. Low-level languages are easier to read than high-level languages
B. High-level languages are easier to write and maintain; low-level languages communicate more directly with hardware
C. High-level languages are made of 0s and 1s only
D. They are exactly the same except for the file extension

A program follows every syntax rule but still displays the wrong result. Which conclusion is most accurate?
A. The IDE has to be replaced
B. The program has no errors at all
C. The syntax is fine, but there is still a mistake in the program that must be found and fixed
D. The CPU is using the wrong language

Which of these is NOT an algorithm?
A. A well-defined procedure to sort names that ends when sorted
B. A step-by-step method to find the largest of three numbers
C. Instructions that loop forever with no way to stop
D. Clear steps to add two numbers that end with the answer

Which statements are TRUE? I. Machine language is binary that the CPU can execute directly. II. Assembly language uses mnemonics and needs an assembler. III. High-level languages are closer to the hardware than machine language.
A. I and III only
B. II and III only
C. I and II only
D. I, II, and III

A team builds a library system. The job is huge, so they split it into borrowing, returning, and searching parts. Which idea are they using?
A. Stepwise refinement / top-down design
B. Debugging
C. Assembling
D. Deployment

Users complain about crashes after a program is released, and the programmer fixes them. Which phase of the programming process is this?
A. Deploy and maintain
B. Create an algorithm
C. Identify the problem
D. Gather requirements

A flowchart and a piece of pseudocode both describe 'read the price, then compute the total'. What do they have in common?
A. Both are written in Java
B. Both are made of 0s and 1s
C. Both can be executed directly by the CPU
D. Both describe the steps of an algorithm without depending on a specific language

A program uses age, Age, and AGE as three different variables. Is this allowed in Java?
A. Yes, because Java is case-sensitive
B. Yes, but only if they are constants
C. No, they are all the same identifier
D. No, uppercase letters are not allowed

A value such as the maximum score must never change after it is assigned. Which keyword should be used?
A. void
B. public
C. static
D. final

What is the value of r?
int r = 17 % 5 + 17 / 5;
A. 5
B. 6
C. 3
D. 2

What is the value of r?
int x = 10;
boolean r = (x > 5) && !(x == 10);
A. It causes an error
B. 10
C. false
D. true

What does this code display?
System.out.printf("%.2f", 3.14159);
A. 3.14
B. 3.1
C. 3.14159
D. 3.00

What does this code print?
System.out.println("Score: " + 5 + 3);
A. Score: 53
B. Score: 5 3
C. Score: 8
D. It causes an error

The program calls nextInt() but the user types the word 'abc'. What happens?
A. An InputMismatchException occurs
B. The Scanner closes automatically
C. The program reads 0
D. The program reads 'abc' as an int

The user types: Maria Cruz. What does the variable s hold?
Scanner input = new Scanner(System.in);
String s = input.next();
A. Nothing (null)
B. Maria Cruz
C. Maria
D. Cruz

What is the exact output of this code?
System.out.println("A\tB");
System.out.println("C\\D");
A. Line 1: AB. Line 2: CD
B. Line 1: A\tB. Line 2: C\\D
C. Line 1: A, a tab, then B. Line 2: C\D
D. Line 1: A B. Line 2: C D

The user enters 4 and 6, and the program shows 10. Which part is the PROCESS step?
A. Showing 10 on the screen
B. Typing the numbers
C. Adding the two numbers
D. Closing the Scanner

What does this code display?
System.out.printf("%d items cost %.2f", 3, 2.5);
A. 3 items cost 2.5
B. 3 items cost 2.50
C. 3 items cost 2.500
D. 2.50 items cost 3

A program must print 'Minor' when age is below 18 and 'Adult' otherwise. Which structure fits best?
A. for loop
B. switch with no cases
C. do-while loop
D. if-else

Which expression evaluates to true?
A. !true
B. false || true
C. !true || false
D. true && false

Which for header prints 'Hello' exactly 5 times?
A. for (int i = 1; i < 5; i++)
B. for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i--)
C. for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++)
D. for (int i = 0; i <= 5; i++)

An array has 5 elements. Which is its valid LAST index?
A. 4
B. 5
C. 6
D. 1

After changeNumber(number) runs, number is still 10. Why?
A. The method turned number into a constant
B. int variables can never be changed
C. Pass-by-value: the method received only a copy of the value
D. Assignments inside methods are always ignored

Which pair of methods shows method overloading?
A. int add(int a, int b) and int add(int a, int b, int c)
B. int add(int a, int b) and another int add(int a, int b)
C. int add(int a, int b) and int sum(int a, int b)
D. void greet() and int count(int n)

What is printed?
int[] numbers = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50};
System.out.println(numbers[1] + numbers[3]);
A. 40
B. 60
C. 4
D. 70

Using n = {{10, 20, 30}, {40, 50, 60}}, what do n.length and n[0].length give?
A. 6 and 2
B. 2 and 6
C. 3 and 2
D. 2 and 3

What is printed?
String w = "Hello";
System.out.println(w.charAt(0) + "" + w.charAt(4));
A. Hello
B. Ho
C. oH
D. H4

What is printed?
String city = "Manila";
System.out.println(city.charAt(city.length() - 1));
A. i
B. M
C. 6
D. a

What is printed?
String s = "Computer";
System.out.println(s.substring(0, 3));
A. Comp
B. omp
C. Compu
D. Com

What is printed?
String s = "Hello World";
System.out.println(s.length());
A. 11
B. 5
C. 10
D. 12

What is printed?
System.out.println(1 + 2 + "A");
A. 3A
B. 12A
C. An error occurs
D. A3

What is printed?
String s = "Computer";
System.out.println(s.substring(2, 5));
A. omp
B. pu
C. mpu
D. mput
